headline: Highest risk is MinerU’s MCP/API surface creating default interaction and data-handling hazards; LlamaFactory is mostly inert but the pair still has medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes MCP Server and API surfaces, so its outputs can be bridged into another agent’s inputs. LlamaFactory is a docs-only LLM framework with no direct I/O surfaces, so the interaction is inferred rather than observed. Because shared-file or MCP bridging is plausible and the rubric says uncertainty escalates, medium is safer than low.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs are forwarded into LlamaFactory prompts or files without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF a shared MCP or API bridge is enabled between the pair, attacker-controlled document text can reach the other agent.
mitigations: Disable any automatic forwarding from MinerU to LlamaFactory.
Add a provenance tag to all MinerU outputs before reuse.
Require human review before LlamaFactory consumes extracted text.
Restrict MCP access to a test-only endpoint.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU processes PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, images, and OCR text, while LlamaFactory is a general LLM framework. Neither profile shows filesystem read/write or secrets handling, but MinerU’s API/MCP surfaces can move document contents into another backend. That makes leakage plausible in default integrations, though not proven from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are sent through MinerU and then reused in LlamaFactory prompts, the data can leave the original workflow.
IF the pair shares an API or MCP bridge, document text may be exposed to the downstream inference backend.
mitigations: Route only redacted samples through the pair.
Turn off any automatic logging of prompts and extracted text.
Keep sensitive documents out of shared workspaces.
Use separate service accounts for each agent.
requires-engineering: enforce per-document access controls and retention limits.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git, or use the network; MinerU also cannot write files or modify git, though it does support MCP and allowlisted egress. With no overlapping mutable filesystem or git writes, direct capability conflict is limited. The remaining overlap is mostly read/transform and API use, so low fits.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable external resource through MCP or an API, they can still contend indirectly.
IF an orchestrator adds shared write permissions not shown in the profiles, conflict severity increases.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the same run.
Avoid shared git or database targets.
Separate their API credentials.
Serialize any writes through one coordinator.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU extracts structured text from documents, and LlamaFactory can consume that text as model input. If LlamaFactory treats MinerU output as authoritative, extraction errors can cascade into downstream summaries or actions. The pair lacks built-in verification in the profiles, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF LlamaFactory uses MinerU output without a verification step, extraction mistakes propagate.
IF downstream automation consumes LlamaFactory’s generated facts, the cascade can affect multiple work products.
mitigations: Insert a verification step between extraction and generation.
Sample-check a few documents manually.
Require citations back to source pages.
Limit downstream automation to draft-only mode.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for extracted fields.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented in either profile, and both are open-source with no secrets handled. The only compliance-relevant surface is MinerU’s allowlisted egress and MCP/API exposure, but there is no evidence of regulated data classes or cross-border transfer. Because the other agent is not implicated by a specific policy gap, low is the safest non-none choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into MinerU and then sent through an external allowlisted endpoint, compliance review is required.
IF deployment policy forbids MCP/API handling of sensitive documents, the pair violates local policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair.
Disable external egress for sensitive runs.
Document retention and deletion settings.
Use a local-only deployment for both agents.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls to the pipeline.
